ranking.rationale: General ideological self-placement is a strong, semantically stable predictor of political behavior across ANES election years and domains. It captures durable policy orientation without directly encoding domain identifiers like year or state, and is less target-leaky than explicit party-ID or party thermometer variables that can act as near-proxies for the label.

Party identification is one of the most stable, semantically central predictors of ANES voting behavior across years and domains. It adds major signal beyond the already selected ideology measure while remaining more robust than year/state, candidate-specific thermometers, or demographic shortcuts that are more likely to encode domain shift or leakage.

Democratic Party feeling thermometer adds strong, broadly stable signal about partisan affect and vote choice beyond ideology and issue importance already selected, while being less tied to specific domains than year/state and less shortcut-prone than demographics or campaign-context variables.

Adds strong, semantically stable partisan affect beyond ideology and issue-position features already chosen. A party feeling thermometer is broadly predictive across ANES years and domains while being less direct leakage than election year/state and less shortcut-prone than demographics.

Age adds broad, semantically stable signal for political behavior and vote choice across ANES election years without directly encoding the train/test domain. It complements the already selected ideology/issue-position features by capturing lifecycle differences in turnout propensity, partisan alignment, and issue prioritization, while being less brittle and less leakage-prone than year, state, party-ID, candidate/party thermometers, or campaign-specific evaluations.

Education is a broadly stable, semantically meaningful predictor of political behavior and preferences across ANES years and domains. It adds complementary signal beyond ideology/partisanship already selected, while being less domain-specific and less leakage-prone than year, state, campaign-exposure, or highly target-adjacent party-evaluation items.

Abortion attitude is a core, durable ideological issue in ANES that remains predictive across election years and domains. It adds substantive policy-position signal beyond the already selected broad ideology/partisanship and demographics, while being less domain-identifying or leakage-prone than year, state, candidate evaluations, or campaign-behavior variables.

Adds a core economic-policy attitude signal that is broadly predictive of political choice and likely to remain meaningful across ANES domain shifts, while being less tied to explicit domain identifiers or demographic shortcuts than year, state, race, or campaign-exposure variables.

Party identification adds strong marginal signal for ANES voting behavior and remains semantically predictive across election years and other domain shifts. It complements the already selected ideology/policy-attitude features by capturing durable partisan alignment, while being less domain-specific and less leakage-prone than year, state, candidate thermometers, or campaign-context variables.

Interest in the elections adds broadly stable signal about political engagement and turnout propensity that should generalize across ANES years and domains. It complements the already selected ideology/issue-position features without relying on brittle domain markers like year, state, or demographics, and is less target-leaky than explicit party-representation or candidate affect measures.

Adds a core economic-policy ideology signal that is broadly predictive of partisan vote choice and likely to remain stable across ANES domain shifts. It complements the already selected spending/aid issue scales with a distinct redistribution dimension, while avoiding stronger domain/leakage risks from year, state, candidate evaluations, or demographic shortcut variables.

Adds broadly stable retrospective economic evaluation beyond existing ideology/party and issue-importance features. Judging government economic policy is a core driver of vote choice across ANES waves and should generalize better than year/state identifiers, demographics, or campaign-exposure variables, while being less target-leaky than explicit party-like/dislike measures.

General national conditions is a broad, semantically stable retrospective evaluation signal that should transfer across ANES train/test shifts better than year/state identifiers, demographics, or campaign-exposure artifacts. It adds complementary valence beyond the already selected issue positions and partisan/ideological measures without being as close to direct party-choice leakage as party feeling thermometers or party-represents-my-views items.

Retrospective economic evaluation is a classic, semantically stable driver of vote choice in ANES and adds signal beyond ideology, party ID, and issue positions already selected. It is less domain-identifying than year/state and less leakage-prone than explicit party-representation or thermometer items.

Gun-control importance adds a strong, policy-based ideological signal that should generalize across ANES train/test shifts better than year, state, demographics, or campaign-behavior variables. It complements the already selected issue-position and partisan-perception features with relatively stable substantive preference rather than domain identifiers or likely leakage.

Perceived government waste adds broad anti-government/efficacy sentiment that is strongly related to political choice yet more stable across ANES years and domains than state, year, demographics, or campaign-exposure variables. It complements the already selected ideology/party-identification and issue-position features with relatively low leakage risk and less redundancy than direct party thermometer or party-representation items.

President thermometer adds strong, broadly stable signal about incumbent-party evaluation and vote choice beyond ideology, issue positions, and demographics already selected, while being less domain-specific than year/state and less brittle than campaign-behavior or demographic shortcut features.

Trust in media adds broadly stable signal about political attitudes and institutional confidence that should generalize across ANES domains, while being less direct leakage of partisan choice than party-like/dislike or party-represents-my-views items and less brittle than year, state, or demographics.

Party feeling thermometer adds strong, broadly stable signal about partisan affect and vote choice beyond ideology, issue positions, and demographics already selected, while being less domain-specific than year/state and less brittle or leakage-prone than campaign-behavior or location features.

This adds a broadly stable civic-attitudes signal that should generalize across ANES years and domains better than year/state/demographic identifiers or campaign-exposure artifacts. Approval of protests captures enduring views about political participation and dissent, complementing the already selected ideology, trust, efficacy, and issue-position features with relatively low leakage risk.

Pre-election voter registration adds strong, generally stable signal about turnout propensity and civic engagement beyond the already selected efficacy/interest variables, while being less domain-specific and less leakage-prone than year, state, or explicit partisan preference items.

Importance of religion is a durable value/identity signal that often predicts partisan choice across elections and regions, adding stable ideological information beyond demographics, issue scales, and political efficacy already selected. It is less likely than year/state or campaign-exposure variables to encode domain shifts, and less directly target-leaking than explicit party-representation or party-thermometer items.

Adds broadly stable civic-engagement/efficacy signal that should generalize across ANES domains and complements already selected political-interest/trust items without relying on year, state, candidate-specific affect, or demographic shortcuts.

Adds broadly stable civic-duty/turnout efficacy signal that should generalize across ANES domains better than year/state, demographics, or highly target-adjacent party-evaluation items; it complements existing political interest/engagement features without relying on brittle domain identifiers or leakage-prone partisan shortcuts.

Adds a broad, semantically stable measure of party representation/alienation that should generalize across ANES domains better than year, state, demographics, or campaign-exposure variables, while being less target-proximal and redundant than explicit party-best or candidate-like measures.

Adds a broadly stable measure of institutional/governance preference that is predictive of partisan choice yet less tied to election-year specifics or direct party-ID leakage than explicit party-representation items, and it complements the already selected ideology/issue-position features with relatively domain-robust signal.

Adds a highly stable, semantically central signal of partisan alignment that should generalize across ANES domain shifts better than year/state or demographic variables. It complements existing ideology/party-feeling measures by directly capturing party representation of respondent views, with less brittleness than campaign-behavior or issue-specific party-performance items.

Adds strong, broadly stable signal about partisan affect that should generalize across ANES train/test shifts better than year, state, demographics, or campaign-contact variables. It complements already selected Democratic and candidate feeling measures by capturing Republican party evaluation directly, improving ideological/party-choice prediction without relying on brittle domain identifiers or demographic shortcuts.

Adds broadly stable civic-norms information about duty to vote that is predictive of political engagement and participation across elections, while being less tied to specific years, places, candidates, or demographic shortcuts than state/year, campaign-media exposure, or explicit party-identification items that are largely redundant with already selected partisan features.

This item captures durable partisan alignment—an especially strong, semantically stable predictor in ANES—while adding less candidate-specific leakage than leader thermometers or campaign-behavior variables. It complements the already selected issue positions, ideology, and party-ID-related measures by directly measuring perceived party-view congruence, which should generalize better across domains than state, year, demographics, or media/contact artifacts.

Political organization membership adds broadly stable signal about political engagement and partisan intensity that should generalize across ANES domains, while being less domain-specific and less leakage-prone than year, state, demographics, or campaign-media exposure variables. It complements the already selected ideology/issue/interest features with a durable behavioral indicator of activism.

Adds a durable ideological/party-issue perception signal not yet fully covered by the selected set: beliefs about which party favors stronger government are broadly predictive of vote choice and partisan alignment across ANES years, while being less domain-specific than year/state and less shortcut-prone than demographics or campaign-contact variables. It complements existing issue and feeling-thermometer features with a stable government-size dimension.

Defense spending preference adds a substantive, policy-based ideological signal that should generalize across ANES train/test shifts better than state, year, demographics, or campaign-exposure variables. It complements already selected issue and party-perception features with a concrete issue-position measure, offering stable marginal predictive value without relying on obvious domain identifiers or brittle participation artifacts.

Adds a broadly stable measure of civic duty/turnout norm that should generalize across ANES years and domains, complementing already selected political interest, efficacy, and participation features without relying on year/state identifiers or sensitive demographic shortcuts. It is less election-specific and less target-leaky than campaign-contact/media exposure items, and more robust across shifts than issue-attribution or demographic variables.

Adds issue-specific party competence on unemployment, a durable economic-valence signal that is highly predictive of vote choice yet less domain-identifying than state/year and less shortcut-prone than demographics or campaign-contact variables; it complements already selected ideology/party-image and economic evaluation features with relatively low redundancy.

Adds broadly stable affective evaluation of the ticket via vice-president thermometer, complementing existing presidential/candidate feeling and issue/party measures with less domain-specific leakage than year, state, media-use, or demographic variables.

This issue-perception item adds substantive policy-based signal about partisan evaluation that is likely to generalize across ANES train/test shifts better than geography, year, or demographics. It complements already selected ideology/party and issue-position features with a distinct environmental dimension, while avoiding stronger domain-ID risk from state, election year, media-use, or campaign-activity variables.

Adds a substantive issue-position/perception signal that is likely to generalize better than geography, year, demographics, or campaign-exposure variables. Given many demographics and ideology/party-related features are already selected, this policy-party association on military spending can still contribute complementary, semantically stable information about partisan belief structure without relying heavily on domain identifiers or post-treatment campaign behavior.

Issue salience about the most important national problem adds broad, semantically meaningful political preference signal that should transfer across domains better than state, year, or demographics. It complements the already selected ideology/party/economic evaluation features by capturing which policy dimension is top-of-mind, while avoiding stronger domain-ID or shortcut risk from election year, state, race, or campaign-behavior/media variables.

Adds broad retrospective national-performance evaluation not yet covered by the selected issue and ideology variables. This kind of incumbent-performance sentiment is generally predictive of vote choice across elections and more stable OOD than state, year, or demographic identifiers, while being less redundant than the campaign-activity and media-exposure items.

Campaign participation adds stable signal about political engagement and turnout propensity that should generalize better across ANES domain shifts than state/year or demographic identifiers. It is less direct leakage than issue-party preference items and complements already selected interest/attention and efficacy-style variables with a distinct behavioral measure.

Campaign participation via attending meetings/rallies adds durable signal about political engagement and activism beyond already selected ideology, issue, and interest measures, while being less domain-specific and less shortcut-prone than year, state, or demographics and less likely to leak through media-era artifacts than internet/media exposure variables.

Campaign donation is a strong, broadly stable indicator of political engagement and partisan commitment that should generalize across ANES election-year shifts. It adds signal beyond already selected ideology, issue, and participation variables, while being less domain-identifying and less shortcut-prone than year, state, gender, race, or media-channel exposure features.

Watching TV programs about election campaigns adds broadly stable signal about political engagement and information exposure that should generalize across ANES domains better than year, state, or demographic identifiers. It is also less redundant than the other remaining media variables because campaign attention is only partially covered by the already selected participation/interest features, while state, year, gender, race, and occupation are more likely to act as domain shortcuts or brittle correlates.

Occupation adds broad socioeconomic structure that can stably relate to political preferences across ANES years while being less direct as a domain identifier than year/state and less likely than campaign-media exposure or demographics to encode brittle period-specific artifacts or shortcut signals.

Adds broadly stable signal about campaign information exposure via radio, which can improve turnout/choice prediction without relying as directly on domain identifiers or demographic shortcuts. It is less time-specific than internet exposure, less behaviorally downstream than displaying a button/sticker, and safer for OOD generalization than year, state, gender, race, or party-on-inflation items.

Magazine campaign-news exposure adds a relatively stable, behavior-based signal about political engagement and information consumption that can generalize across ANES train/test shifts. It is less likely than state or year to encode domain identity, less directly shortcut-like than gender/race, and less target-proximal than issue-party preference. It also complements already selected campaign-contact and media-use variables without being fully redundant.

Internet campaign-information exposure adds broadly useful behavioral/media-consumption signal that can help explain political engagement and vote choice beyond the already selected ideology, issue, and participation variables. It is less likely than state or election year to act as a direct domain identifier, and less problematic than gender or race as a demographic shortcut; it should transfer more stably across ANES train/test shifts.

Adds a policy-specific partisan evaluation signal that is likely predictive of vote choice beyond the already selected ideology/issue items, while remaining more semantically tied to political preferences than domain identifiers like year/state or demographic shortcuts like gender/race.

Gender can add some stable, semantically meaningful signal for political attitudes and vote choice beyond the already selected issue, ideology, and participation variables, while being less domain-specific than election year or state and generally less problematic as a brittle shortcut than race/ethnicity.

Campaign participation via displaying a candidate button/sticker is a behaviorally grounded indicator of political engagement and partisan commitment that should remain predictive across domains. It adds signal beyond already selected turnout/interest/party-related items while being less likely than state, election year, or race/ethnicity to act primarily as a domain identifier or demographic shortcut.

Race/ethnicity can add some residual, semantically meaningful signal about political preferences beyond the already selected ideology, issue, religion, income, education, and urbanicity variables. It is less directly a train/test domain identifier than election year or state, though it should still be downweighted relative to attitudinal features because it can act as a demographic shortcut.

Election year can capture broad, semantically meaningful shifts in national political context that affect vote choice and issue salience across respondents, adding some stable signal beyond the already selected attitudinal variables. State is more likely to act as a domain identifier and encode geography-specific distributional artifacts, making it less suitable for OOD generalization.

State is primarily a domain/location identifier in ANES and is likely to capture region-specific survey, political, and demographic artifacts that shift across environments rather than stable individual-level signal. Given the strong attitudinal and demographic features already selected, its marginal value for robust OOD generalization is low and potentially harmful, but it is the only remaining candidate.
